facts.statement: Cretornis lived approximately 92 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Czech Republic.
facts.quote: Cretornis is a pterosaur genus from the late Cretaceous period (Turonian stage) of what is now the Jizera Formation in the Czech Republic, dating to about 92 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cretornis were discovered in 1880 by quarry workers in Zářecká Lhota, Czech Republic, who were extracting gravel for road repair.
facts.quote: The fossils were discovered in 1880 by workers at a sandstone quarry in Zářecká Lhota near the town of Choceň, who were getting gravel to repair a local road.

facts.statement: A local resident named Mrs. Tomková alerted pharmacist and collector František Hlaváč to the fossil discovery.
facts.quote: A certain Mrs. Tomková, a croupier from Choceň, then alerted František Hlaváč, a Choceň pharmacist and fossil collector, to the find.

facts.statement: Professor Antonín Frič originally identified the fossils in 1881 as a toothed bird the size of a swan and named the species Cretornis hlavaci.
facts.quote: In 1881, Frič identified it as a prehistoric toothed bird the size of a recent swan and named it as the type species Cretornis Hlaváči.

facts.statement: The specific name 'hlavaci' honors the collector František Hlaváč.
The holotype fossils of Cretornis are currently housed in the National Museum in Prague.
facts.quote: Today, the holotype fossils of this pterosaur are stored in the National Museum in Prague.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including a complete humerus, ulna, radius, wrist, and two wing finger phalanges.
facts.quote: It is a partial skeleton lacking the skull. It contains a complete humerus (upper arm bone), an ulna, radius, wrist and two phalanges of the wing finger.

facts.statement: Scientists later realized that the fossils originally identified as a bird actually belonged to a pterosaur.
facts.quote: Afterwards it was realized that the find represented some pterosaur.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with relatives, the wingspan of Cretornis hlavaci is estimated to be between 1.5 and 1.6 meters.
facts.quote: Based on comparison with its relatives, the wingspan of C. hlavaci has by Averianov been estimated at 1.5 to 1.6 m.

facts.statement: The humerus of Cretornis is approximately 3 inches long.
facts.quote: The humerus is 3 in in length.

facts.statement: A unique derived trait of Cretornis is that the distal part of its humerus has a diamond-shaped cross-section.
facts.quote: In 2015, Averianov indicated a single autapomorphy, unique derived trait: the distal part of the humerus has a diamond-shaped cross-section.

facts.statement: In the nineteenth century, Cretornis was classified as a species within the genus Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: Cretornis was classified as a species in the genus Ornithocheirus in the nineteenth century.

facts.statement: A 2018 analysis by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues placed Cretornis within the family Nyctosauridae, a position that contradicts its placement within Azhdarchoidea.
facts.quote: In 2018, paleontologist Nicholas Longrich and colleagues had recovered Cretornis within the family Nyctosauridae, in a more derived position than Alamodactylus and Volgadraco, this contradicts its position within the Azhdarchoidea.

facts.statement: Detailed comparisons of wing bones suggest Cretornis belongs to a non-azhdarchid azhdarchoid, likely a member of the group Neoazhdarchia.
facts.quote: Aunque ha sido clasificado con frecuencia como una especie del géneroOrnithocheirus, las comparaciones más detalladas de los huesos del ala muestran que estos pertenecían a un azdarcoideo no azdárquido, probablemente un miembro del grupo Neoazhdarchia.

facts.statement: Cretornis is likely more advanced than the Thalassodromidae and shares several features with Montanazhdarcho.
facts.quote: Es probable que sea más avanzado que los talasodrómidos, y comparte varias características en común con Montanazhdarcho.

facts.statement: The time range for Cretornis is estimated from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)
